summary: The island looks worse to a player than it did three sessions ago. Every new mechanic leaves something behind: purple and yellow domino slabs from the dayfall fence off the meadow, huge matte grey spheres hang over it in the orbit view, and Pickles has been lost 2.6 km out under the sea. The two new films do not deliver. 'My shadow quits' is a faint grey smear seen past a tree trunk, a remake of session 95's 'My shadow ran off'. 'The island has a ring' is a diagonal streak of beads seen from a drone. The traced still is clean and soft, but it is still plastic under one sun, and 17:00 looks like noon.

lighting.why: Night in the raster has some mood: warm lamp pools by the cottage and a dusk horizon. But the 17:07 path traced still (reviews/p0121/traced.png) is flat white noon: no low warm sun, no long shadows, no glowing thing lighting its surroundings. Every film this session is flat midday too.

materials.why: The traced still is all diffuse or plastic: trees, fences, slabs, mushrooms. The ring's junk is plain matte spheres in orange, blue and pink. In the shadow film the pond is an opaque green floor with lily pads, nothing like the sea's water. The jelly (s118) is still the only material that is the point of anything.

world.why: Down from 6. The dayfall leaves rows of untextured purple and yellow slabs standing across the meadow and along the paths (jumpin.png, orbit-17h-b.png, overview). Giant grey spheres hang a few metres over the meadow (orbit-17h.png, orbit-17h-b.png, and at the bottom of every wide frame of ring-3). The black shore band is still there (follow-17h.png). The overview is a carpet of tiny scattered props with no clearings. The eye-level view is still a grey slab.

props.why: 52 generated assets in the catalog, and the cottage, easels, TV and workbench read well. But the newest additions are primitives: domino slabs, sphere junk, sphere clouds.

creatures.why: Shapes and faces are still charming up close: the pig, the sheep, the crab's hat. But one of the ten is lost: Pickles sits at (-2136, -1449, -1.4), under the sea and far off the island (the dark void tile in motion/creatures.png). Half of the close-ups on the creatures sheet show a fence or tree instead of the creature.

animation.why: 9 of 10 move well (most were asleep). Pinchy snaps 0.27 m in one frame, runs at 8.2 m/s and ends up inside a bush (motion/motion-strip.png is 22 frames of green leaf). In the ring film Pinchy's throw is a speck. The shadow film is 9 s of slow dolly with almost nothing moving.

fun.why: Jump in has a lot of verbs (17 keys: swallow, throw, tip, shadow...), and the island runs its own events (choir, circle dance). But nothing new this session is playable, and the key bar is so long it runs off the left edge of the view ('SD walk').

wow.why: Down from 6. 'My shadow quits' is the idea of plugins/shadow.jl from session 95 again, and it came out worse: a grey smudge you have to be told about. Both posts say on the page that they failed. The ring's idea is good, but the film shows a diagonal streak, not a ring. Nobody would share either one.

camera.why: Follow at night: a giant orange barrow fills half the frame and Lumi is a label on pink foliage (now.png). Follow at 17:00: Lumi is cut by the bottom edge and the camera looks at the sea and the black band (follow-17h.png). The motion camera sat inside a bush for 2 s. The shadow film opens with a tree trunk covering the left fifth. The eye-level progress shot is a grey wall.

ui.why: The panel reads well. The Jump in key bar overflows the left edge of the view. The night follow view has firefly halos as big as UI buttons floating over the faces.

style.why: Soft clay creatures and plush trees next to hard flat purple slabs, matte grey balls and confetti props: three looks fighting each other.

performance.why: Sandbox frame median 5.35 ms, p95 12.5 ms, a steady 30 fps with 10 creatures and 252 props.

findings.title: Pickles is lost 2.6 km out under the sea: bring strays home
findings.what: One of the ten friends is gone. Pickles the Snootle is at (-2136, -1449, -1.4), under the water and far beyond the island. In the creatures sheet it is a pig floating in a dark blue void. The ring fix in s121 brings ring riders home, but other things (drift, ring, seesaw, throws) can still strand a creature.
findings.where: live sandbox: game.world.creatures; reviews/p0121/motion/creatures.png row 5 left
findings.suggestion: One general rule in the core, not per plugin: any creature more than ~30 m from the island centre, or below sea level for more than a few seconds, swims or flies home with a funny line ('Where did everybody GO?'). Make the walk back a little moment of its own.
findings.done_when: After an hour of sandbox time, every creature's position is within 30 m of the island and above z = 0; Pickles shows up on its own tile in live_motion's creatures sheet.

findings.title: Clear the dayfall's leftover slabs off the meadow, or make them real tiles
findings.what: The dayfall's tiles stay standing as rows of untextured purple and yellow boards. They fence off the meadow and the paths and stand right next to Lumi. From the orbit they look like construction hoardings, not a toy.
findings.evidence: jumpin.png: eight purple slabs taller than Lumi; orbit-17h-b.png: yellow slab lines across the whole middle
findings.suggestion: Once a run has fallen, the tiles should be gathered away (a friend carries them off, or they sink into the grass) within a minute. While they stand, give them a painted face or a generated tile mesh with wood grain and a coat in the trace, so a row of them is a picture.
findings.done_when: A screenshot from the orbit camera 5 minutes after a dayfall shows no standing slabs; a close screenshot of a standing run shows a textured tile, not a flat colour.

findings.title: Giant matte grey spheres hang over the meadow and fill the camera
findings.what: Two or three huge grey-white balls, several metres across, hang a few metres over the meadow by the easels. In the orbit view they cover half the frame. The same white dome blocks the bottom of every wide frame of the ring film. They are not props: no prop above z = 2 is bigger than 2.5.
findings.where: orbit camera; reviews/p0121/orbit-17h.png, orbit-17h-b.png; ring-3 overview frames 6 to 12
findings.evidence: orbit-17h.png: a lavender sphere over half the view; orbit-17h-b.png: two grey balls over the easels
findings.suggestion: Find the plugin (clouds, cloudshapes, bubbles or ring). Low clouds belong out at sea and well above the trees. If they are meant to be low fog banks, make them a volume in the trace and soft in the raster, never a matte ball in front of the lens.
findings.done_when: Orbit-camera screenshots at 3 times of day show no grey sphere bigger than a creature in the lower 2/3 of the frame.

findings.title: The black band round the shore is still there live
findings.what: A dark grey band runs between the turquoise shallows and the white sand all along the shore. It is the fourth review in a row that names it.
findings.where: follow camera near the shore; reviews/p0121/follow-17h.png
findings.evidence: follow-17h.png bottom half: a black band between the sea and the sand
findings.suggestion: Look at the terrain's underwater skirt and the sea's depth tint where they meet. The shallows should fade from turquoise into wet sand, darker sand only a hand wide.
findings.done_when: follow-17h-style screenshot at the shore shows sea → wet sand → dry sand with no band darker than the wet sand.

findings.title: Eye-level view: no white slab or grey wall, on a tilted island too
findings.what: The eye-level progress shot is still a grey sheet across the lower 2/3, under a strip of green and sky. It is the same shot as the last three reviews.
findings.suggestion: Clamp the eye-level camera above the terrain and the water plane at the point it looks from, after the seesaw tilt. Frame a creature or a landmark in the lower third.
findings.done_when: The next progress eye-level.png shows grass, creatures and props from head height, with no flat grey or white surface over more than 10% of the frame.

findings.title: Game cameras stop looking through pines, barrows and bushes
findings.what: Follow at night: an orange barrow fills the right half of the view and Lumi peers out of pink foliage. Follow at 17:00: Lumi is cut off at the bottom and the camera stares at the sea. The motion camera was inside a bush for 2.2 s. The shadow film's first frames have a tree trunk over the left fifth.
findings.evidence: now.png (barrow), follow-17h.png (Lumi cut), motion-strip.png (22 of 24 frames green leaf)
findings.suggestion: Cast a ray from the subject to the camera and pull the camera in front of whatever it hits, or fade those meshes. Keep the subject between the lower third and the middle of the frame, with its face visible.
findings.done_when: Ten follow-camera screenshots 5 s apart at day and night: the followed creature's face is in frame in all ten, and no prop covers more than 25% of any of them.

findings.title: Goal 2: release one film you would sign, not one more failed first take
findings.what: Eight films in a row went up with captions that admit they failed: 'came out a blob', 'small and far off', 'filmed from too far away', 'crashed my GPU'. Goal 2 has not moved in 35 reviews. The shadow film repeats session 95's idea. The ring film shows a streak.
findings.evidence: site posts 'My shadow quits (first try)', '(second try)'; releases/ newest is 2026-11-24
findings.suggestion: Spend two sessions on one film: the jelly swallowing Pinchy or the rope knot, shot close at eye height at golden hour with a cut or two in VideoEditor, 128+ spp with OIDN. Put it in world/releases/ with its note.
findings.done_when: A new folder in world/releases/ holds a film whose motion sheet shows the creatures at least 1/4 of the frame high in most frames, with sun below 25° (long shadows), and no frame where a prop covers the lens.

findings.title: Pinchy snaps, runs 8 m/s and walks into bushes
findings.what: Pinchy jumps 0.27 m in one frame, moves at 8.2 m/s, and ends up inside a bush where the camera loses it. The s118 vibration finding is still open on top of this.
findings.evidence: live_motion: 'Pinchy: jumps 0.27 m in one frame at 0.9 s', 'moves at 8.2 m/s'
findings.suggestion: Cap the crab's speed at a scuttle (~2 m/s), ease into and out of moves, and keep its paths outside bush and tree footprints.
findings.done_when: live_motion lists Pinchy under 'Moving well' in three runs in a row.

todos.why: The frame failure happened once (today 03:11) and not again in 15 hours of logs.
Not checked this review; hats and rods still need a look up close.
Jump in still opened looking past Lumi's back at the slabs, not a clean chase view.
The face hill shows in none of the 8 views or 3 films; the camera, shore and slab findings matter more.
No moth blur and no misplaced speech in 8 screenshots this review.
The drift is no longer filmed or shown; reopen if it comes back.
The TV still has no glass or brass in the trace.
Not replayed this review; still a gameplay bug the player would hit.
At night the fireflies are big pale discs over the faces in the follow view (now.png), still beads, not glow.
todos.title: Fireflies that glow: small warm points that light the grass, not big discs over faces

todos.why: my-shadow-quits-3 still opens on a popped first frame (a dark blue blot, jump 0.096 at 0.04 s).
The jelly is the best material idea on the island and is still murky.
No orange flecks in 8 screenshots or the 3 films this review.
The ring film shows a diagonal streak of plain spheres; the close-up is still to do.
plugins/shadow.jl (s95) already lets the shadow run off live; a second version of the same trick costs a session a player would not notice.

engine.what: Hikari's SunLight is a hard delta light, so a shadow cast from 15 m up is still razor sharp and has no penumbra to show off. A sun with an angular radius (a disk light) would give the soft, long golden-hour shadows a path tracer is for.
engine.evidence: journal 2026-11-26 17:59: 'The sun is a hard delta SunLight in Hikari'

engine.what: The worker keeps state between jobs (UNDERLIGHT[:force]), which ruined two films in one day (ring take 2, shadow take 2 came out at night).

process: The author is still starting one new mechanic per session and filming it once, and this time it left visible damage. The dayfall slabs stay standing, grey spheres hang over the meadow, a creature was lost at sea, and the shadow idea was a remake of session 95's. 'Finish rather than add' from the last review was not followed: the shore band (4 reviews), the eye-level slab (4 reviews), the camera through foliage and Pinchy's jitter are all still open, and two of three sessions went to films that were posted as failures. Goals: 1 (interactions) moved only through the ring rider fix. 2 (release) has not moved. 3 (physics) moved a little with the ring. 4, 6 and 7 (rendering, light at every hour, path tracer materials) are stuck: every film is flat noon in plastic. 5: Lumi's mood is bored, joy 1.0, loneliness 1.0, and 9 of 10 friends were asleep while it reviewed. 8 is weakened by repeats. The next three sessions should clean the island (slabs, spheres, strays, shore band, eye level), then make one golden-hour film of the jelly or the rope, close up, and release it.
